Synopsis:
Player speaks with Kagha, the secret Shadow druid. Various paths of conversation reflect whether Kagha's actions led to a child's death or not. She may be neutral/Machiavellian or pure evil, depending.

Cluster Contexts:
- DEN_ShadowDruid_Leader.json: You have just exposed Kagha as a secret Shadow Druid and the grove is in open crisis: Olodan’s Cloakwood contingent has arrived, ordinary animals are shifting into shadow-touched druids, and the circle is being pressed to purge “tainted” intruders. Off-screen there was an incident over the Idol of Silvanus — Kagha claims she recovered it and resumed a protective rite, and a tiefling child accused of stealing the idol is at the center of the dispute (either under guard in a druidic “court” or already harmed, depending on prior choices). Kagha is a trusted, politically important member of the circle who is visibly torn between loyalty to the grove and the shadow teachings; she can be argued with but will harden if the child has been maimed or killed. The scene thus sets up a forced choice: try to sway Kagha away from the shadows or prepare to fight Olodan and his newly transformed druids while other circle members react.
- DEN_SacredPond_BirdSender.json: This dialogue can take place in two different states. In the first, Apakusis is short and defensive. The grove's ranking leader, Kagha, has gathered support to close off the grove to outsiders with an intense ritual. She doesn't trust Kagha, and quietly despairs to see her grove turn to such measures.In the second state, the ritual has been stopped. She's shocked at the revelation that Kagha had been involved with Shadow Druids, and is having trouble accepting it.The player finds this druid speaking to a bird in the druid grove.
- DEN_ShadowDruid_SelfReflection.json: Following Kagha's dialogue, if druid player asked about the rite and has not already discovered the shadow druid connection, they experience a self-reflection. There is more to this tale; you should search Kagha's quarters. Journal entry to search her quarters appears.
- DEN_SacredPond_RitualDruid2.json: This dialogue can occur in three different states: In the first, Kerrick is in a trance, chanting a spell that will cover the druid grove in thorns. In the second, the ritual has been stopped after a druid named Kagha was exposed as a Shadow Druid. Kerrick is furious - he feels betrayed by Kagha, and doesn't quite care if she's been killed.In the third, a group of goblins that had threatened the grove has been dealt with and the grove is considered safe again. In this state, Kerrick has calmed down a good bit - now that the danger's passed, he's seeing things with a bit more clarity. The player always encounters Kerrick around a sacred druid pool.
- DEN_ShadowDruid_Denouncing.json: You have just exposed Kagha as a Shadow Druid, and as you confront her the rats in the grove visibly shift into shadow-druids — a Cloakwood contingent led by the sleazy, slobbering Olodan has arrived and openly welcomes the circle into their fold. Olodan accuses Halsin and the circle of letting "untouchables" corrupt the grove and immediately orders Kagha to purge the tainted, starting with you as the snitch. Kagha is a trusted member of the grove and is clearly torn — her voice trembles and she may be persuadable, but convincing her to renounce the shadow teachings will be very difficult, especially if the child mentioned earlier was already killed. The scene forces a choice: try to sway Kagha away from the shadows (with strong roleplay checks), or fight Olodan and his newly transformed druids while Rath and other circle members react to the betrayal.

Dialogue Excerpts (up to 3 samples, ordered):
Sample 1:
- Kagha: A grey dwarf - in our grove, on this day. A sign. Or rather, a gift. (node 89)
- Kagha: Who better to understand a watchful broodmother than one who hails from... below? (node 52)
- Kagha: Who better to understand a watchful broodmother than a beloved child of Lolth? (node 35)
- Player: I'd have killed the thief outright. (node 36)
- Kagha: Yes. Yes. This could be the true way of Silvanus. (node 176)
- Kagha: The viper bares her fangs defending her brood. It is only right that she strike the killing blow. (node 192)
- Kagha: The others might consider this sacrilege. But we know the truth: it is necessity. (node 100)
- Kagha: I took back the Idol of Silvanus and the rite has resumed. We will seal the grove. Free from harm. Free of intruders. (node 118)
- Kagha: No matter. I took back the Idol of Silvanus and the rite has resumed. We will seal the grove. Free from harm. Free of intruders. (node 201)
- Player: Attack. (node 143)

context: You have just exposed Kagha as a secret Shadow Druid and the grove is in open crisis: Olodan’s Cloakwood contingent has arrived, ordinary animals and some druids are shifting into shadow-touched forms, and the circle is being pressured to purge “tainted” intruders. Off-screen there was an incident over the Idol of Silvanus—Kagha claims she recovered it and resumed a protective rite—and a tiefling child accused of stealing the idol is central to the dispute (that child may be under guard or already harmed depending on prior choices). Kagha is a politically important, trusted leader who is visibly torn between loyalty to the grove and the shadow teachings, and she frames harsh actions as necessary preservation (viper/brood imagery appears in her lines). The scene forces a choice: try to persuade her to renounce the shadow teachings or prepare to fight Olodan and his newly transformed druids; Kagha will be much harder to sway if the child has been maimed or killed.
